document_check.note: Peng S-W, Wang C-Y, Lin S-Y, et al. (2023) 'Subjective Cognitive Complaints: Comparing the Relation between Self-Reported Versus Informant-Reported Subjective Cognitive Complaints and Cognitive Performances in Cognitively Unimpaired, Mild Cognitive Impairment and Populations with Dementia', J Prev Alz Dis 10(3):562-570. It is a cross-sectional memory-clinic study: the same 12-item questionnaire was given to participants and informants, and self-reported SCC was not associated with cognitive performance in any diagnostic group (Table 3).

cited_result: Adjusted linear regressions of total neuropsychological z score on the self-reported total SCC score, controlling for age, sex, education, family history, informant SCC, GDS and anxiety/depression rating. Self-report was not associated with cognition in the whole sample (B -0.001, 95% CI -0.217 to 0.215), CU (B -0.088), MCI (B 0.068, 95% CI -0.18 to 0.315) or dementia (B -0.273) (Table 3, page 6; discussion page 7).
tool_reason: The cited result is an association between two measures taken at one time point (self-reported complaints and measured cognition) within diagnostic groups, which fits the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: The age criterion, the grounds for attending and the exclusion criteria are stated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: The main inclusion criterion was age greater than 50 years old, who had either memory concern or no memory concern but were willing to take questionnaire and cognitive assessments due to personal interests. The exclusion criteria were history of major brain trauma, brain tumor, stroke, epilepsy, alcoholism, major psychiatric illness, medication or other systemic diseases that affect cognitive function.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The setting, recruitment period and group demographics (Table 1) are reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: We enrolled participants from a memory clinic in a tertiary medical center in Taiwan from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2018 and assessed them with clinical review and cognitive tests.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: The exposure (self-reported SCC) comes from a published Mandarin questionnaire administered in interview, with acceptable internal consistency reported. External validity is supported only by citation.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Participants were interviewed in the hospital by neurologists. Subjective cognitive complaints were assessed by 12 questions using the Mandarin self-assessment questionnaire, proposed by Cheng CH et al (13-15). (p2) / The analysis for the total of 12 questions showed very good Cronbach’s alpha scores: 0.81 for the participants’ SCC scores and 0.845 for the informants’ SCC scores. (p4)

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: Dementia uses NIA-AA criteria; early and late MCI use ADNI-style memory cut-offs on WMS-LM.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: The diagnosis of dementia with ACS is based on the criteria of the National Institute on Aging and the Alzheimer’s Association for probable AD dementia (26). The diagnosis of early and late MCI is based on the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohorts (27), with impaired episodic memory function documented by the Chinese version of the Wechsler Memory Scale – Logical memory subscale (WMS-LM) (Delayed Paragraph Recall).

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education, family history and mood/anxiety are named as covariates.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: As for determining the association of SCC scores and neuropsychological tests, linear regression models were performed, controlling age, gender, education, family history and anxiety/depression scores.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Multivariable regression was used, stratified by diagnostic group (Table 3).

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: Table 3. Linear regression of cognitive performance (via total z score) in different study groups

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: Standard neuropsychological tests were given by trained staff and z-standardised against CU participants. The way the total z score in Table 3 was built from domain composites is not fully described.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Neuropsychological assessments were conducted by trained psychologists and research assistants. (p2) / For further analysis, we compute z score for each test within the domains, by standardizing against the CU participants. Domain composite scores were computed by averaging z scores within each domain. (p3)

domains.rationale: Linear regression suits the question, but several things are unreported or unaddressed. The number analysed in each model is not given; only 1,028 of 1,536 participants had informants, and handling of the rest is stated only for the dyad comparisons. Self and informant scores, and GDS and the anxiety/depression rating, enter the same model, so the self-report coefficient is conditional on informant report. The within-stratum analyses use groups defined by cognitive cut-offs, which restricts the outcome range.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: For the comparison of participants’ and informants’ SCC scores, we analyzed only the data for which both scores were available. (p3) / Table 3 models include both 'SCC_total_P' and 'SCC_total_I' together with 'GDS' and 'Anxiety/depression rating score' (p6); no model N is reported.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: 7 Yes, 1 Unclear)
overall_rationale: Confounders were identified and handled by multivariable regression, and the outcome and condition were measured with standard instruments and criteria, so no item that triggers high risk is 'No'. Statistical analysis is Unclear for three reasons: the analysed N and missing-informant handling are unreported; self and informant scores are mutually adjusted; and strata defined by cognitive cut-offs restrict range. By the review's rule, this gives some concerns.

applicability.rationale: Help-seeking memory-clinic attendees at a single Taiwanese tertiary centre; the authors state the results may not extend to community-based individuals (page 8).
